column1: # ZAP baseline policy — which findings block the build.
# Format: <rule-id>  <IGNORE|WARN|FAIL>  <name>   (tab separated)
# The build fails on FAIL only. WARN is printed on every run and blocks nothing,
# because the scan runs with -I.
# Every line below is the result of running the scan, reading the output, and
# deciding. Nothing here is a guess, and nothing here is IGNORE — an ignored
# rule is a rule nobody will ever look at again.
# The app reflects ?name= into the response body without escaping it. That is
# safe only because every response carries Content-Type: text/plain AND
# X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. Remove the second one and a browser is free
# to sniff the body as HTML, at which point the reflection is stored XSS.
# CLAUDE.md 1.1 requires both headers. TestHelloIsNotHTML asserts them, and
# gosec flags the reflection statically (G705). This is the third check, and the
# only one that looks at the running binary from the outside — it would catch the
# header being lost in the Dockerfile, in a middleware, or by a proxy, none of
# which a unit test or a source scanner can see.
# Measured on 2026-09-10, both directions, before this file was committed:
#   hardened build  -> PASS  (65 PASS,  0 FAIL, 2 WARN)
#   nosniff removed -> WARN  (64 PASS,  0 FAIL, 3 WARN)   <- the one line differed
# Set to FAIL so that difference stops the build instead of scrolling past.
# ── 90004 / 10049 — reported on every run, deliberately not blocking ─────────
# Both appear on the hardened build too, so promoting either to FAIL would fail
# the pipeline permanently on the current, correct code. Both are also real, and
# both are fixed by a header the app does not yet send:
#   90004  Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy — cross-origin read protection
#          (Spectre-class). Low value for a text/plain ClusterIP service with
#          no Ingress in front of it, which is why it is not in the 1.1 contract.
#   10049  Storable and Cacheable Content — no Cache-Control on a response that
#          reflects user input. There is no shared cache in this path today; put
#          one in front and this becomes a cross-user leak.
# Left at WARN rather than IGNORE: the honest state is "seen, understood, not
# worth a contract change yet", and WARN keeps them on screen so that stays a
# decision rather than a silence. Fixing them means amending 1.1 first.
